clue.text: Astaire regularly eats fish

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the name Astaire, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: to eat a meal is to dine, so eats gives dines

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire, the dancer, has a habit of tucking into fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the alternate letters S, A, R from Astaire; DINES follows.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small oily fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Tremulous tree in ski resort

explanation.surface: A quivering tree stands in a skiing town.
explanation.definitionFit: The trembling poplar has leaves that quiver in a breeze, and Aspen in Colorado is a famous ski town.

clue.text: Try a dialect when posing as lower class?

indicators.note: posing as something means taking on a different shape, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone affects an accent to pass themselves off as working class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower class' reads as the social sense, but a lower here is something that lows, like a cow; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows that are milked make a herd of animals that moo, a whole class of lowing creatures.

clue.text: Denial, for example, accepted by the body politic

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the short piece goes within the larger one

parts.note: the body politic is a people organised as a state, a nation

explanation.surface: A refusal, say, is taken on board by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or contradiction is the act of saying no to something.

clue.text: Stay-at-home doctor alters treatment, supplying first-aid item

parts.note: to stick in is to stay at home rather than go out
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

indicators.note: treatment means the letters get worked over and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A housebound doctor changes the remedy and hands over a bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive dressing for small cuts is a standard thing in a medicine kit.

clue.text: Harry and Virginia in Vogue

indicators.note: in places the state abbreviation inside the word for vogue

parts.note: something in vogue is all the rage
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Two people, Harry and Virginia, appear in a fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb, to harass or lay waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to raid and plunder, laying a place waste.

clue.text: Keep putting volunteers in control

indicators.note: putting one piece in another means the volunteers go inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keep a tight rein
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to power by putting reservists in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to something and not give it up is to hang on to it.

clue.text: Compete with little girl on horseback

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Vi is a short form of the girl's name Violet
the back of the word horse is its last letter, E

explanation.surface: A small girl rides a pony in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to contend or strive against others.

clue.text: Female novelist has it in for former Labour leader

indicators.note: has it in means the novelist holds the word it inside

parts.note: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian novelist, author of Cranford

explanation.surface: A woman writer has a grudge against an ex-leader of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has it in for' reads as bearing a grudge; it actually puts IT into GASKELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Gaitskell led Britain's Labour Party from 1955 until his death in 1963.

clue.text: Suddenly reveal source

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly discloses where a piece of news came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring a surprise is to produce it without warning, and a spring is where a stream rises, its origin.

clue.text: Doughty, popular time-traveller -one-dimensional?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative
I is the Roman numeral for one
D stands for dimensional, as in 3-D

explanation.surface: A celebrated time-traveller is brave but rather shallow as a character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time-traveller' looks like a single sci-fi figure; it splits into T and REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughty person is brave and unafraid, fearless in the face of danger.

clue.text: Just feasible-fifty years later

parts.note: something that is on can be done, as in that's not on
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Something might just be possible half a century on.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and merely both mean no more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Assume midshipman is to avoid exertion

parts.note: to take it that something is so is to assume it
Mr Midshipman Easy is the title hero of a novel by Captain Marryat

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer is presumed to be dodging hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 sea novel by Frederick Marryat, a classic of British naval fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and not overdo things means steering clear of strain or effort.

clue.text: Shrill preparation for personal adornment

explanation.surface: A high-pitched shriek accompanies getting ready to wear jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing high sound hurts the hearing, and making a hole in the lobe readies it for studs or rings.

clue.text: A sweet biscuit or a half roll dunked in wine

indicators.note: dunked in means put inside, so the short pieces go into the wine

parts.note: Macon is a French wine from the Maconnais in Burgundy

indicators.note: half asks for the first two of the four letters of roll

explanation.surface: Choosing between a biscuit and half a bread roll soaked in wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small almond cake or cookie made with egg white, a kind of sweet treat.

clue.text: Now pitch spare tent

indicators.note: to pitch a tent is to put it up, so the letters are erected in a new order

explanation.surface: A camper is told to put up the extra tent immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: At this moment, currently, is the same as at the time being.

clue.text: Whistle-blower, rounding point, discloses maritime hazard

indicators.note: rounding means going round, so the referee's letters enclose the compass point

parts.note: a ref, or referee, blows the whistle in football
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An informant who sails round a headland exposes a danger at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant; it is the football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral just below the surface is a danger to ships.

clue.text: In December it reanimates an African

indicators.note: In says the answer is held within the run of words December it reanimates

explanation.surface: Something is brought back to life in the last month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Eritrea, a country on the Red Sea in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: It's exactly the same as saliva

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a thing is identical to spittle.
explanation.definitionFit: The spit of someone is their exact likeness, a double, and spit is also the fluid in the mouth.

clue.text: A little bit mad in April etc

indicators.note: mad means crazed or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly crazy in the spring months and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny piece or speck, the smallest fragment of something.

clue.text: Generator repaired by Monday

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A power unit will be fixed by the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that turns motion into electric current, as on a bicycle wheel.

clue.text: Seasoning clearly set out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction states plainly how a flavouring is laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: A condiment of salt mixed with ground celery seed, used to flavour food.

clue.text: Island resort's contribution to parliamentary democracy

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seaside town plays its part in the system of elected government.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryde is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a holiday town on the Isle of Wight, so an island resort; the possessive 's links the definition to the wordplay as 'has'.

clue.text: Took risks with diamonds, diamonds, diamonds

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for the suit of diamonds
ice is slang for diamonds
D again, the abbreviation for diamonds in card play

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on the red suit three times running.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition suggests one meaning thrice; the middle one is slang ICE, the outer two the card abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice with death is to gamble with danger, so this means gambled recklessly.

clue.text: Bird seen before dawn may be cardinal

indicators.note: seen before means the first piece is placed ahead of the next one

parts.note: cardinal is a bright red colour, from the robes of a cardinal
dawn is the start or beginning of something

explanation.surface: A bird spotted before daybreak might be a red cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like the American songbird; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of the thrush family with a reddish tail.

clue.text: Turf for lawman?

explanation.surface: Grass is asked for on behalf of a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of grass with its roots is a clod of lawn, and the Sod of Sod's law, the rule that whatever can go wrong will, is jokingly a lawmaker.

clue.text: European number in this French show?

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A European figure appears in a French display.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to reveal or display it plainly.

clue.text: Workshop making poker with odd bits of iron

parts.note: stud is a form of poker

indicators.note: odd bits of asks for the first and third letters of the word iron

explanation.surface: A smithy turns out a poker from scraps of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poker' suggests the fireside tool; it is the card game, stud poker.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's workroom is a place where things are made.

clue.text: Defector, extremely awkward, in Greene novel

indicators.note: in places the outside letters of awkward inside the rearranged Greene
novel means new, so the letters of Greene are made into a fresh word
extremely asks for the first and last letters of the word awkward

explanation.surface: A turncoat behaves very clumsily in a Graham Greene story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greene novel' suggests a Graham Greene book, but 'novel' is the anagram signal, making RENEGE; 'extremely' picks the outside letters of awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor or turncoat who deserts a cause or country.
